meta.title: Frictionless Insurance Assistance
s1.tagline: An AI co-pilot for insurance advisors, in chat and by voice, built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
s1.note: Sample demo: Awesome Insurance, its products and all customer data are fictional.
s2.title: Why Insurance Advisors Need AI
s2.c1.title: Complexity & Information Overload
s2.c1.li1: Insurance documents are complex, jargon-heavy, and difficult to interpret quickly
s2.c1.li2: Advisors manage hundreds of products across multiple providers — impossible to know everything
s2.c1.li3: Manual comparison is time-consuming and error-prone
s2.c2.title: Lost Momentum & Revenue
s2.c2.li1: When customers ask questions, advisors often say "let me get back to you" and wait for the insurer — losing momentum and trust
s2.c2.li2: Customers expect instant, personalized answers — not callbacks days later
s2.c2.li3: Advisors miss cross-sell/upsell opportunities due to lack of holistic coverage visibility
s2.c3.title: Competitive pressure
s2.c3.body: Digital-first insurers and aggregators are raising the bar — advisors who can't deliver instant, informed answers lose deals to those who can.
s3.title: Frictionless Insurance Assistance
s3.intro: An AI-powered advisory tool that transforms how insurance advisors interact with customers — making every conversation informed, instant, and customer-centric.
s3.c1.title: Document Intelligence
s3.c1.body: Upload insurance policies from any insurer — the tool ingests, understands, and makes them queryable instantly
s3.c2.title: Real-time Q&A
s3.c2.body: Advisors can answer customer questions on the spot, with the sources shown — no more waiting for insurers to come back with clarifications
s3.c3.title: Product Comparison
s3.c3.body: Compare products across providers with carrier financial-strength ratings, a customer handout PDF, and a competitor brochure you upload on the spot
s3.c4.title: Coverage Gap Analysis
s3.c4.body: Automatically identify what is missing in a customer's coverage, with the estimated dollar exposure of each gap
s3.c5.title: Multi-channel
s3.c5.body: Works via chat for digital interactions or voice for live customer calls
s3.c6.title: Works for All Customers
s3.c6.body: Existing portfolio reviews or new prospect onboarding
s3.c7.title: Applications That Fill Themselves
s3.c7.body: The application form opens mid-conversation, for ten Awesome products, and populates as the advisor and customer talk — in chat or by voice
s3.c8.title: Show Your Sources
s3.c8.body: Every answer cites the documents or web pages behind it, and the same product, company, and competitor documents can be browsed in the app
s3.c9.title: Ten Languages
s3.c9.body: Interface and AI answers in English, 日本語, 한국어, 简体中文, Español, Français, Deutsch, Bahasa Melayu, ไทย, Bahasa Indonesia
s4.title: Value for Insurers
s4.c1.title: Customer Centricity
s4.c1.body: Complex insurance documents decoded instantly — advisors focus on the customer, not paperwork
s4.c2.title: Increased Revenue
s4.c2.body: Cross-sell/upsell through automated coverage gap identification
s4.c3.title: Competitive Advantage
s4.c3.body: Advisors armed with real-time knowledge of competitor products by simply uploading their policy documents
s4.c4.title: Zero Wait Time
s4.c4.body: Eliminate the "let me check and get back to you" — answer questions in real-time during the conversation
s4.c5.title: Faster Onboarding
s4.c6.title: Improved Retention
s4.c6.body: Proactive coverage reviews for existing customers
s4.c7.title: Advisor Productivity
s4.c7.body: Reduce research time from hours to seconds
s4.c8.title: Consistent Experience
s4.c8.body: Standardized advice quality across every advisor — and across ten languages from one knowledge base
s5.title: How Advisors Use It
s5.c1.title: Upload & Understand
s5.c1.body: Upload any insurer's policy documents → AI extracts key terms, coverage, exclusions, and benefits
s5.c2.title: Existing Customer Review
s5.c2.body: One-click meeting brief → coverage gaps with dollar exposure → recommend products → answer questions instantly
s5.c3.title: New Prospect Onboarding
s5.c3.body: Needs assessment → competitive comparison → tailored recommendation
s5.c4.title: Real-time Advisor Support
s5.c4.body: During customer calls (chat or voice), AI provides instant answers — no more callbacks
s5.c5.title: Competitive Positioning
s5.c5.body: Know what competitors offer and position your products effectively
s5.c6.title: Simplify Complexity
s5.c6.body: Turn complicated insurance language into clear, customer-friendly explanations
s6.title: Start the Day Knowing Who to Call
s6.c1.title: Today's priorities
s6.c1.body: The home screen ranks the customers who need attention, with every reason and one click to Draft email or Annual review. The rules run in code, so the list is the same every time
s6.c2.title: A note when you want one
s6.c2.body: After a voice session, one click drafts a Summary, Concerns and Next actions note from the conversation. The advisor edits it and presses Save; nothing is stored unless they do
s6.c3.title: One login per line
s6.c3.body: Life, General and Health advisors see their own customers, and the comparator and gap analysis switch by line. A customer with no Awesome policy is treated as a prospect
s6.c4.title: Gaps and forms from the profile
s6.c4.body: One click gives a coverage-gap analysis for Life, General, Health or all, or opens any of the ten application forms filled in with the customer's details
s6.c5.title: A form that keeps its answers
s6.c5.body: Opened from the profile or from the assistant, it is the same form. Answers typed or spoken stay put when it is closed or the advisor moves between pages
s6.c6.title: Test files for every customer
s6.c6.body: Download a sample third-party policy and upload it to see the document read into structured fields the advisor confirms before anything is saved
s7.title: Ready Before the Customer Sits Down
s7.c1.title: Meeting prep in one click
s7.c1.body: A structured brief — customer snapshot, goals, discovery questions, products to discuss, objection handling, and a close — built from the profile, notes, other insurers' policies, promotions, and competitor material
s7.c2.title: Indicative pricing
s7.c2.body: Premium estimates for all ten products, calculated from rate tables in code and never by the model, with an affordability check against 10% of income. Always an estimate, never a quote
s7.c3.title: Notes that stay with the customer
s7.c3.body: Life events and interactions are kept on the customer's record. The assistant can add a note when asked, and never deletes one
s7.c4.title: Carrier strength at a glance
s7.c4.body: AM Best, S&P, and Moody's ratings sit beside every compared product, on screen and in the customer PDF
s7.c5.title: A competitor brochure on the spot
s7.c5.body: Upload a competitor's PDF brochure, compare it side by side with Awesome products, and let it delete itself within a day
s7.c6.title: Beyond the documents
s7.c6.body: General insurance questions get a live web search, with page titles and links shown. Awesome products, prices, and competitors never come from the web
s8.title: The Application Fills Itself
s8.intro: When the advisor and customer agree to start an application, the form opens beside the conversation and populates from it. In chat or by voice, the advisor keeps talking and fields land as they speak.
s8.c1.title: Ten Awesome products
s8.c1.body: Term, whole, universal, and variable life, critical illness, health, home, auto, travel, and disability — each with a published form of sections, fields, types, and mandatory flags
s8.c2.title: Answers carry over
s8.c2.body: All ten forms share the applicant details, and the four life forms share 18 of about 20 fields. Switch product mid-conversation and nobody is asked their date of birth twice
s8.c3.title: Confidence you can see
s8.c3.body: High-confidence answers fill green; anything less fills amber with a "Looks right" confirmation. Nothing is hidden from the advisor
s8.c4.title: Known details prefilled
s8.c4.body: Fields already on the customer record arrive filled and labelled as such. Precedence is manual > conversation > profile, so typed corrections are never overwritten
s8.c5.title: The schema never touches the model
s8.c5.body: Forms are read from S3 server-side and pushed straight to the browser. The model only receives the field paths — no wasted tokens, no invented fields
s8.c6.title: Guarded by design
s8.c6.body: A field write is rejected unless its path exists in the form actually open, and refused outright if no form is open. A printable PDF is one click away, and Send for Signature saves the finished application. Sending it again replaces that save instead of adding a duplicate
s9.title: Built to Be Trusted
s9.c1.title: Consent comes first
s9.c1.body: In voice, nothing is remembered, filled in, or transcribed until the advisor confirms the customer agreed. Declining ends the session and saves nothing
s9.c2.title: Transcripts that expire
s9.c2.body: Voice transcripts go to a private store, are readable only by the advisor who held the conversation, and expire after a day
s9.c3.title: Answers you can check
s9.c3.body: Sources are built from what the tools actually returned, so the AI cannot invent a citation
s9.c4.title: One shared guardrail
s9.c4.body: The same content, personal-data, and denied-topic policy (legal and tax advice) applies to chat, comparison, recommendations, and document reading. Voice runs under its system prompt and tool checks
s9.c5.title: Estimates, not promises
s9.c5.body: No binding quotes, approvals, or claim payouts. Prices are labelled indicative and calculated in code
s9.c6.title: The advisor stays in control
s9.c6.body: Policies and notes are saved only when the advisor asks or confirms, deletion stays in the app, and low-confidence document readings are checked field by field. Every tool call is tied to the signed-in advisor's own token, so one advisor's assistant can never act as another
s10.title: End-to-end on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
s10.svg.frontendJwt: Cognito JWT only — no IAM creds
s10.footnote: Models: Claude Haiku 5.5 (chat, comparator, recommendations, document and brochure reading) · Nova 2.5 Sonic (voice). One shared Bedrock Guardrail gates the six Claude surfaces; voice is not covered. Before every tool call, the gateway checks the advisor's own sign-in token. Five CDK stacks; every AgentCore resource is stable CloudFormation.

n1.b1: Introduce the product: an AI co-pilot for insurance advisors, in chat and by voice.
n1.b2: It is built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and works in ten languages.
n1.b3: This is a sample demo: Awesome Insurance, its products and all customer data are fictional.
n1.b4: Agenda: the challenge, the solution, the benefits, daily use, the application flow, trust, then the architecture.

n11.b1: Consent comes first in voice: nothing is remembered, filled in or transcribed until the advisor confirms the customer agreed.
n11.b2: Voice transcripts go to a private store, are readable only by the advisor who held the conversation, and expire after a day.
n11.b3: Sources are built from what the tools returned, so the AI cannot invent a citation. There are no binding quotes, approvals or claim payouts.
n11.b4: One shared guardrail covers content, personal data and denied topics such as legal and tax advice. Policies and notes are saved only when the advisor asks or confirms.
n12.b1: The React + Vite app runs on CloudFront and holds only a Cognito JWT, no IAM credentials.
n12.b2: The text runtime uses Strands with Claude Haiku 5.5. The voice runtime uses Strands BidiAgent with Nova 2.5 Sonic over WebSocket.
n12.b3: The AgentCore Gateway offers 12 targets and 20 tools over MCP, and its request interceptor checks the advisor's token before every tool call. Memory is per customer with a 90-day TTL.
n12.b4: One shared Bedrock Guardrail covers the six Claude surfaces, not voice. Voice traces carry timings and tool names, not conversation content. Five CDK stacks.
